title: The read-only query log and docs commands are kb MCP tools
goal: the kb MCP server lists kb_querylog (digest, status, show) and kb_docs (selfdoc stale, section and map, check.py, rag.py eval) tools, read-only annotated, that return what the commands print

clauses.clause: the kb MCP server lists kb_querylog (digest, status, show) and kb_docs (selfdoc stale, section and map, check.py, rag.py eval) tools, read-only annotated, that return what the commands print

gates.question: How are kb_docs commands named and which options of querylog.py and kb_docs commands do the tools take?
options: kb_docs commands stale, section, map, check (check.py) and eval (rag.py eval); each command takes only options on a closed list, so digest --hook, --store and eval --write-shares stay on the command line
free argv after the command, with a list of refused options
gates.recommendation: kb_docs commands stale, section, map, check (check.py) and eval (rag.py eval); each command takes only options on a closed list, so digest --hook, --store and eval --write-shares stay on the command line
gates.answer: kb_docs commands stale, section, map, check (check.py) and eval (rag.py eval); each command takes only options on a closed list, so digest --hook, --store and eval --write-shares stay on the command line

gates.question: How do the two tools run the scripts and return a finding exit?
options: a subprocess per call; stale, check and eval answer their text with (exit 1) last when they exit 1, other non-zero exits are tool errors; output is redacted and cut at 60000 characters
in-process like kb_backlog; every non-zero exit is a tool error
